source.author: verg
source.text: Da sternere corpus loricamque manu valida lacerare revulsam semiviri Phrygis et foedare in pulvere crinis vibratos calido ferro murraque madentis.
source.text_original: Da sternere corpus / loricamque manu valida lacerare revulsam / semiviri Phrygis et foedare in pulvere crinis / vibratos calido ferro murraque madentis.'
source.text_english: Let them cast down the body and tear apart with their strong hand the torn-off breastplate of the half-man Phrygian, and defile in the dust the locks, still waving, wet with hot iron and myrrh.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: da mergere Graios insanamque ratem: nil me mea pignora tangunt, tantum hominum compesce minas, dum litora iuxta Thessala necdum aliae viderunt carbasa terrae.
reuse.text_original: da mergere Graios / insanamque ratem: nil me mea pignora tangunt, / tantum hominum compesce minas, dum litora iuxta / Thessala necdum aliae viderunt carbasa terrae.
reuse.text_english: Let the Greeks and the mad ship be plunged; my own pledges do not move me at all. Only restrain the threats of those men, while the shores of Thessaly are still near, and no other land has yet seen the sails.
